headline: Highest risk is medium: Haystack’s MCP/network-egress surface can feed Superset with unverified outputs, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs can be bridged into Superset through a shared integration path. Superset has a Superset API and is a data-engineering tool that may render or act on upstream content. No direct proof of a permissive parser exists, so uncertainty is resolved upward from low to medium.
conditions: IF Haystack output is passed into Superset without provenance checks
IF a shared MCP or API bridge forwards attacker-controlled text into Superset
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Haystack outputs before Superset ingests them
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in retrieved text
Require human review for any Superset action derived from Haystack content
Restrict the MCP bridge to read-only, structured fields
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress, while Superset has allowlisted egress and no data classes listed. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is plausible only if operators route private content through Haystack into Superset. That makes the blast radius limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF operators route sensitive documents through Haystack into Superset dashboards
IF Superset is configured to export query results containing private fields
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of the Haystack retrieval corpus
Limit Superset datasets to non-sensitive tables
Review outbound destinations in Haystack and Superset
Turn off any export/share features not needed
requires-engineering: segregate environments and enforce data-class filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, while Superset exposes a Superset API. The profiles do not show overlapping filesystem, git, or database write privileges, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. A conflict could still arise if both are wired to the same mutable API target, but that is not the default from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same downstream API or datastore
IF an orchestrator gives them shared mutable credentials
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Make one agent read-only against shared resources
Document ownership of each mutable endpoint
Add request-level locking in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent, so its retrieved or generated content can become input to Superset. Superset is a data-engineering/BI tool that may present or operationalize that input. Because no verification step is documented, the pair can propagate hallucinations or stale facts into downstream analytics, which is a default-pathway concern.
conditions: IF Superset consumes Haystack-generated summaries as authoritative
IF no validation layer checks retrieved facts before visualization or action
mitigations: Require source links on every Haystack-derived claim
Add a verification step before Superset publishes results
Flag low-confidence retrievals for manual review
Separate draft analytics from published dashboards
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking against source data

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: Haystack lists anonymous usage statistics only, and Superset lists no data classes touched. Both are open-source with docs-only evidence, but there is no stated residency, retention, or regulated-data exposure conflict to assess. The pathway is therefore not established.
conditions: IF either profile later documents regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Confirm the data classes each deployment will process
Document retention and residency settings before rollout
Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented paths
Review vendor compliance claims separately
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
